sights.n: Okinawa Peace Memorial Park & Prefectural Peace Memorial Museum (平和祈念公園)
sights.w: The main memorial to the Battle of Okinawa, on Mabuni Hill where the fighting ended in June 1945. The museum traces the lead-up, the battle and the rebuilding; outside, the Cornerstone of Peace lists every fallen soldier and civilian of every nationality.

sights.n: Himeyuri Peace Museum (ひめゆり平和祈念資料館)
sights.w: Museum beside the Himeyuri Monument, telling the story of the schoolgirls drafted as nurses into army cave hospitals in 1945, most of whom died. Opened 23 June 1989.

sights.n: Former Japanese Navy Underground Headquarters (旧海軍司令部壕)
sights.address: Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan (Navy HQ park, south of Naha)
sights.w: Several hundred metres of hand-dug tunnels and rooms that served as the Imperial Navy's command post in 1945; the walls still bear the shrapnel marks of the officers' last stand.

sights.n: Okinawa Churaumi Aquarium (沖縄美ら海水族館)
sights.address: Ocean Expo Park, Motobu, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Widely rated Japan's best aquarium, at the tip of the Motobu Peninsula. Its Kuroshio Tank — one of the largest in the world — holds whale sharks and manta rays.

sights.n: Cape Manzamo (万座毛)
sights.w: Grassy clifftop above the Onna coast with the elephant-trunk rock arch; one of the island's most-visited viewpoints.

sights.n: Tokei Beach & Heart Rock, Kouri Island (ティーヌ浜)
sights.w: The north-shore cove of 'Love Island' Kouri, reached by the long Kouri Ōhashi bridge, where the heart-shaped rock formation stands in the shallows.

sights.n: Furuzamami Beach, Zamami Island (古座間味ビーチ)
sights.w: Zamami's best beach, a 20-minute walk from the port: 'Kerama blue' water and reef straight off the sand; holds two Michelin Green Guide stars per the village.

sights.n: Sunset Beach, Chatan (サンセットビーチ)
sights.w: Artificial-bay beach beside Mihama American Village on the west coast, about 250 m of sand facing the sunset.

sights.n: Zanpa Beach, Yomitan (残波ビーチ)
sights.w: West-coast swimming beach beside Cape Zanpa, reached by airport limousine bus to the cape resort.

sights.n: Okinawa World & Gyokusendo Cave (おきなわワールド 玉泉洞)
sights.w: Culture park built over Gyokusendo, a 5 km limestone cave (850 m open) — the longest in the south and second-longest in Japan — with a craft village of old houses and a habu snake museum.

sights.n: Yomitan Yachimun no Sato Pottery Village (やちむんの里)
sights.w: Lane of red-tile workshops and climbing kilns founded after Living National Treasure Jiro Kinjo moved his studio here in 1972; around 45–50 potters, with shops selling cups, plates and shisa.

sights.n: Cape Zanpa & Lighthouse (残波岬)
sights.w: The main island's westernmost cape: 30 m cliffs and Okinawa's tallest lighthouse (31 m), a classic sunset spot, with a park and giant shisa statue.

sights.n: Ōjima Island (奥武島)
sights.w: Tiny bridge-linked fishing island off Nanjō, famous for cheap fresh-fish and seaweed tempura stands and its many cats.

sights.n: Yonaha Maehama Beach (与那覇前浜)
sights.w: Seven kilometres of white sand on Miyako's south-west tip, facing Kurima Island — the beach that usually tops rankings of Japan's best.

sights.n: Kabira Bay (川平湾)
sights.w: Turquoise-to-emerald bay on Ishigaki's north coast, a national Place of Scenic Beauty inside Iriomote-Ishigaki National Park; swimming is banned, so see it by glass-bottom boat over the black-pearl farms.

sights.n: Tatami-ishi, Kume Island (畳石)
sights.address: Ōjima, Kumejima, Shimajiri District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: About a thousand pentagonal and hexagonal andesite columns, each 1–1.5 m across, exposed at low tide on the south shore of Ōjima, bridged to Kume Island — a Miocene lava field that looks like tatami mats.

sights.n: Hiji Falls (比地大滝)
sights.address: Kunigami Forest Park, Hiji, Kunigami, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: The main island's tallest waterfall (25.7 m), reached by a forest trail and suspension bridge through the Yanbaru subtropical woods from the Kunigami campground.

sights.n: ASMUI Spiritual Hikes (former Daisekirinzan, 大石林山)
sights.w: Trails through jagged limestone karst near Cape Hedo, a place of prayer for some 600 years — renamed ASMUI Spiritual Hikes.

sights.n: Cape Hedo (辺戸岬)
sights.w: The northernmost point of Okinawa Island: jagged limestone cliffs where the East China Sea meets the Pacific, with Yoron Island on the horizon and the Yanbaru-kuina observatory on the hill behind.

sights.n: Tsuboya Yachimun-dōri pottery street (壺屋やちむん通り)
sights.w: The Ryūkyū Kingdom's ceramics quarter: a 400 m stone-paved street between Kokusai-dōri and Route 330 lined with potteries, kilns and shops selling yachimun ware and shisa, with wheel-throwing classes.

sights.n: Mihama American Village (美浜アメリカンビレッジ)
sights.w: Reclaimed-land entertainment district with a Ferris wheel, Depot Island's colourful facades, US-style diners and boutiques — the clearest expression of Chatan's base-town melting pot.

sights.n: Koza Gate 2 Street (コザ ゲート通り)
sights.w: The street running to Kadena Air Base's Gate 2, Okinawa's live-music strip since the 1960s–70s: rock, blues and Latin bars alongside Okinawan folk; home of the November International Carnival.

sights.n: Kaichū-dōro sea causeway (海中道路)
sights.w: Five-kilometre road laid across turquoise shallows from the Katsuren Peninsula to Henza, then bridged on to Hamahiga, Miyagi and Ikei — the island-hop drive of central Okinawa.

sights.n: Amamichu, Hamahiga Island (アマミチュー)
sights.w: Rocky islet off 'God's Island' Hamahiga, revered as the tomb of Amamikiyo and Shinerikiyo, the creator deities of the Ryūkyū myths; reached on foot across a short causeway.

sights.n: Ikei Beach, Ikei Island (伊計ビーチ)
sights.w: Reef-sheltered beach on the farthest of the Kaichū-dōro islands, with some of the clearest water reachable by car from the main island.

sights.n: Mount Omoto (於茂登岳)
sights.w: At 525.5 m the highest peak in Okinawa Prefecture, rising from the Omoto range on Ishigaki's north; a forest trail climbs to views over Kabira and the reef. Paired with Kabira Bay as a national Place of Scenic Beauty.

sights.n: Taketomi Island & village (竹富島)
sights.w: Fifteen minutes by ferry from Ishigaki: a preserved Ryūkyū village of coral-stone walls, red-tiled houses and white-sand lanes travelled by water-buffalo cart — a national Important Preservation District since 1987 — ringed by Kondoi Beach.

sights.n: Kurima Island & Kurima Ōhashi (来間島)
sights.w: Small island reached by the 1.7 km Kurima Ōhashi from Miyako's south-west, with café stops and Nagamahama beach looking back across to Maehama.

sights.n: Ikema Island & Ikema Ōhashi (池間島)
sights.w: Fishing island off Miyako's northern tip, reached by the 1.4 km Ikema Ōhashi over shallow turquoise reef.

sights.n: Tōri-ike, Shimoji Island (通り池)
sights.w: Two collapsed-cave sinkholes in the coral of Shimoji's west coast — 75 m and 55 m across, linked to each other and the sea by an underwater cave — the 'dragon's eyes', a national Natural Monument and a celebrated cave dive.

sights.n: Miyara Dunchi (宮良殿内)
sights.w: Residence of a Ryūkyū-kingdom official built in 1819 in the style of Shuri samurai houses — an Important Cultural Property with a rock garden that is a Place of Scenic Beauty; still lived in, so viewed from outside.

sights.n: Hoshizuna-no-hama star sand beach, Iriomote (星砂の浜)
sights.address: Uehara, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Small north-shore Iriomote beach whose 'sand' includes millions of star-shaped foraminifera skeletons; snorkelling over the reef straight off the beach.

sights.n: Yonekoyaki Shisa Park, Ishigaki (米子焼工房 シーサー園)
sights.w: Roadside garden behind the Yonekoyaki pottery workshop crowded with giant, psychedelic, pop-art shisa lion-dog sculptures.

sights.n: Hacksaw Ridge (Maeda Escarpment, 前田高地)
sights.w: The Urasoe escarpment where medic Desmond Doss lowered wounded men down the cliff in May 1945; trails lead to Needle Rock and the Doss point above the city.

sights.n: Kokusai-dōri (国際通り)
sights.w: Naha's 1.6 km main street of shops, cafés, bars and awamori stores, rebuilt so fast after 1945 it was nicknamed the 'Miracle Mile'; the gateway to Makishi market, Tsuboya and the arcades, and the stage for the city's big festivals.

sights.n: Kinjō-chō Ishidatami-michi stone-paved road (金城町石畳道)
sights.w: About 300 m survive of the c.1522 limestone-paved royal road that ran south from Shuri Castle, winding steeply between old stone walls and red-tiled houses.

sights.n: Okinawa Prefectural Museum & Art Museum (沖縄県立博物館・美術館)
sights.w: The prefecture's flagship museum in Shintoshin: Ryūkyū history, nature and crafts from prehistory to the US era, with a modern Okinawan art wing.

sights.n: Sakaemachi Market (栄町市場)
sights.w: Showa-era covered market by Asato station: groceries by day, and after dark a warren of tiny bars and izakaya where locals drink on stools in the alleys.

sights.n: Sunayama Beach (砂山ビーチ)
sights.w: Cove reached over a tall sand dune 4 km north of Hirara, framed by a natural rock arch — one of Miyako's signature beaches.

sights.n: Cape Higashi-hennazaki (東平安名崎)
sights.w: A 2 km finger of land at Miyako's south-east tip, strewn with tsunami boulders, ending at a 1967 white lighthouse with a 320° ocean panorama.

sights.n: Irabu Ōhashi Bridge (伊良部大橋)
sights.w: Opened 31 January 2015: at 3,540 m Japan's longest toll-free bridge, arcing over turquoise shallows from Miyako to Irabu Island.

sights.n: Valley of Gangala (ガンガラーの谷)
sights.w: Collapsed-cave valley of banyan-draped limestone opposite Okinawa World, where remains linked to the 18,000-year-old Minatogawa people were found; visits by guided tour only.

sights.n: Bise Fukugi Tree Road (備瀬のフクギ並木)
sights.w: Kilometre of sandy lanes in Bise village tunnelled by centuries-old fukugi windbreak trees, five minutes from Churaumi; walk or cycle to Cape Bise.

sights.n: Fukushū-en Garden (福州園)
sights.w: Walled Chinese garden opened in 1992 for Naha's sister city Fuzhou, built with materials shipped from Fujian — pagoda over a waterfall, ponds and moon gates in old Kume, the Chinese scholars' quarter.

sights.n: Hate-no-hama sandbar, Kume Island (ハテの浜)
sights.address: off eastern Kume Island, Kumejima, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: A 7 km ribbon of pure white sand bars in the open sea east of Kume Island, reached only by a 20-minute boat ride — no shade, no buildings, just reef and sky.

sights.n: Nago Central Park / Nago Castle Park (名護城公園)
sights.w: Hillside park on the old Nago gusuku site — the only place in Okinawa on Japan's list of 100 best cherry-blossom spots (deep-pink kanhi-zakura in late January) — with the Tenjo lookout over Nago Bay.

sights.n: Nago Pineapple Park (ナゴパイナップルパーク)
sights.w: Kitsch pineapple-themed park on Route 84 with self-driving pineapple carts through the plantation and tastings of pineapple everything.

sights.n: DMM Kariyushi Aquarium (DMMかりゆし水族館)
sights.address: iias Okinawa Toyosaki, Toyosaki, Tomigusuku, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Okinawa's second-largest aquarium, in the iias Toyosaki mall near the airport: projection and AR-enhanced tanks, penguins, and a walkway over a big shark-and-ray tank.

sights.n: Ie Island & Mt Gusuku 'Tatchu' (伊江島 城山)
sights.w: Flat island a 30-minute ferry from Motobu, dominated by the 172 m rock spire of Gusuku-yama ('Iejima Tatchu') — climb for views back to the Motobu Peninsula.

sights.n: Sesoko Island & Sesoko Beach (瀬底島)
sights.w: Small bridged island off Motobu with one of the main island area's clearest swimming beaches, facing Minna and Ie islands.

sights.n: Mt Yaedake cherry-blossom road (八重岳桜の森公園)
sights.w: Japan's first cherry blossoms of the year: about 7,000 deep-pink kanhi-zakura line a 4 km road up the main island's second-highest mountain, with a festival from mid-January.

sights.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Itoman (具志川城跡)
sights.w: Gusuku perched on sea cliffs at the southern tip of the island, surrounded by sea on three sides — a National Historic Site with sweeping coastal views.

sights.n: Itokazu Castle Ruins (糸数城跡)
sights.w: Fourteenth-century gusuku at 180 m — the highest castle ruin in the south — its curved limestone walls built to guard Tamagusuku; views over the southern coast.

sights.n: Tamagusuku Castle Ruins (玉城城跡)
sights.w: The oldest castle on Okinawa Island, said to have been built by the creator goddess Amamikiyo; its arched gate in the natural rock frames the solstice sunrise. National Historic Site.

sights.n: Chinen Castle Ruins (知念城跡)
sights.w: Compact cliff-top gusuku with a pair of arched stone gates, believed to be the second-oldest castle in the Ryūkyūs; near the sacred Chinen-Ukka spring. National Historic Site.

sights.n: Gushikawa Castle Ruins, Kume Island (具志川城跡)
sights.w: Fifteenth-century gusuku on a cliff-bound headland in Kume Island's north-west, four low-walled enclosures above the East China Sea; National Historic Site since 1975.

sights.n: Tsuboya Pottery Museum (那覇市立壺屋焼物博物館)
sights.w: Municipal museum on Yachimun-dōri with some 7,000 pieces — from a 6,700-year-old shard through Ryūkyū-kingdom wares to today's masters — plus a preserved climbing kiln.

sights.n: Tamatorizaki Observation Point, Ishigaki (玉取崎展望台)
sights.w: Hilltop platform on Ishigaki's east coast looking over Cape Tamatori, Ibaruma Bay, the hilly Hirakubo peninsula and the reef.

sights.n: Yubu Island water-buffalo crossing (由布島)
sights.address: Komi, Taketomi, Yaeyama District, Okinawa, Japan
sights.w: Tiny island off Iriomote reached by water-buffalo cart across a shallow sandy strait, often to a sanshin song from the driver; a botanical garden and cafés on the island.

sights.n: Iriomote Island jungle & mangroves (西表島)
sights.w: Okinawa's second-largest island, about 90 % jungle and mangrove — part of the 2021 UNESCO natural World Heritage site and home of the critically endangered Iriomote cat; explored by river cruise and kayak (Urauchi River, Pinaisara Falls — the prefecture's tallest at 55 m).
